# SystemVerilog generated by ROHD

[ROHD](https://github.com/intel/rohd) generates SystemVerilog from Dart. A
lint finding on that SystemVerilog points at a generated line, which is not
the line you edit. When ROHD has recorded where each signal and instance was
created, LintCrux shows that **Dart source** next to the SystemVerilog location,
and **Go to Dart source** opens it in your editor.

This is from LintCrux 1.2, and is labelled **ROHD 0.7 or later (source
tracing)**: the source-trace file it reads is written by ROHD 0.7 and later, and
only when source tracing is on. For the whole path from ROHD to LintCrux, see
[ROHD + EDACrux](rohd-and-edacrux.md).

## Turn tracing on in your ROHD flow {#flow}

Call `SourceTracer.activate()` before the design is built, and write the trace
file after the SystemVerilog:

```dart
SourceTracer.activate();
final top = Top(/* ... */);
await top.build();

final sv = SystemVerilogService(top);
File('build/Top.sv').writeAsStringSync(sv.output);
TraceService(top, svService: sv, packageRoot: Directory.current.path)
    .write('build');   // writes build/Top.flc.json
```

`Top.flc.json` is the source-trace file ("FLC": file, line, column). Version 6
is the version read here. The SystemVerilog also carries `// ROHD:` comments,
which LintCrux uses when no source-trace file is available.

## Where LintCrux looks {#find}

For each `.sv` file in the project, LintCrux reads:

1. the source-trace files named in the `.lintcrux` file under
   `perEngineOptions.rohd.sidecar`, and
2. every `*.flc.json` in the same folder as the `.sv` file.

A trace file applies to the SystemVerilog file it says it was written for (the
name match ignores case), so `Top.flc.json` beside `Top.sv` works with no
configuration. The one-file and the one-module-per-file layouts both work.

```json
"perEngineOptions": {
  "rohd": { "sidecar": ["build", "other/Alu.flc.json"] }
}
```

Each entry is a file or a folder; relative paths are against the project root.

## What you see {#see}

Select a finding on a generated line. Under the SystemVerilog location the
inspector shows **Dart source (ROHD 0.7 or later)**: the Dart file, line and
column, a note on how it was found, and the callers.

- **Exact**: the line declares, drives or connects a signal or an instance that
  ROHD recorded. The location is the Dart line that created it. For an
  instance, the callers include where it was instantiated.
- **Enclosing block or instance**: a line that only reads a signal, such as
  `if(valid_bit)`, has no record of its own. LintCrux follows the block or
  statement around it (an `always_comb`, a multi-line instance) and shows the
  Dart line that created that.
- **From the `// ROHD:` comment**: used when no trace file is found, for the
  same two cases. ROHD does not write comments inside `always_comb` or on port
  declarations, so a trace file finds more.

A finding in a file with no trace data shows no Dart source and is otherwise
unchanged. The SystemVerilog location stays the finding's location, so
baselines and waivers are not affected.

The Dart location is also written into exported SARIF, in the result's
`properties`, under `lintcrux.rohdSource`.

## When the trace file cannot be used {#problems}

A trace file of a version other than 6, one that is not valid JSON, and one
that cannot be read are each reported once as a warning and then ignored. The
lint run is never failed or slowed by it: from the command line the warning is
in the diagnostics, and the `// ROHD:` comments are still used.

If the generated files were moved after ROHD wrote them, LintCrux finds the
Dart package by looking for the Dart file above the trace file and above the
SystemVerilog file, and falls back to the nearest folder with a `pubspec.yaml`.

## Limits {#limits}

- Only the primary location of a finding is mapped, not its related locations.
- LintCrux reads the SystemVerilog and the trace file; it does not run ROHD.
